newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares rise sharply in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares rise sharply in brisk trade.

text.p: Egyptian shares rose sharply on Tuesday in very active trade which a broker said would continue for some time.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index jumped 3.61 points to close at 286.41 while turnover almost doubled to 93.2 million pounds ($27.4 million).
But some brokers found it normal, as the market was performing well.
"The market is in equilibrium, with a general uptrend," said Mohamed Magdy of EFG-Hermes brokerage. "Such active trade should be expected from now on as ususal."
Broker Hany Hosny of Megavest agreed, saying "the market is stable."
Heliopolis Housing and Development was the most active share for the third day in a row, far outpacing other shares on the top ten list in terms of turnover.

The Egyptian government last month said it was auctioning five percent or more of its shares in the partially-privatised Heliopolis to at least one strategic investor. The state currently owns 72.86 percent of the firm.
But brokers said the government was selling the shares through the stock exchange.
"The (state's) holding company is selling shares through brokers," said a broker, who declined to be named.
Shares worth 26.29 million pounds of Heliopolis were traded but the share ended unchanged at 320.
Heliopolis said on Monday it nearly doubled net after-tax profits in the financial year 1995/96 to 61.35 million pounds from 34.07 million in the previous year.
Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN was the second most acitve share and ended at 140.00 pounds, up 27.99.
"The share is doing well since the government has said it would sell off a part of its stake in the firm through global depositary receipts (GDR)," Hosny said.
Amriyah Cement was the third most active share, with shares worth 3.43 million changing hands. It finished 2.50 up at 70.50 pounds.
"There is good demand for this share after the government offered 10 percent of its stake for sale," Magdy said.
Popular millers were still among the most active shares.
Central and Western Delta Flour Mills ended unchanged at 85.00, East Delta Flour Mills added 2.00 to end at 52.50.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 433.59 from 431.15 points on Monday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 200.66 from 197.31.
Of the 76 shares traded, 25 rose, 22 fell and 29 were unchanged.
$1 = 3.4 pounds
